first.rationale: Simplifying onboarding directly addresses the 4% completion decline and may also recover activation, with two inherited findings indicating durable early-adoption gains. Verify both records before final commitment and evaluate qualified revenue and retention—not completion alone—to guard against downstream value loss.

mid.rationale: Run a standard experiment shortening the self-serve onboarding flow. This directly addresses the 4% completion decline, while verified evidence shows higher completion, faster time-to-value, improved activation, and positive qualified-revenue impact. Monitor 30-day retention and qualified revenue because the SMB signup simplification record showed a small retention decline and its segment generalizability is uncertain.

final2.rationale: Switch this cycle’s experiment to a tightly targeted pricing response for price-sensitive SMB accounts showing credible churn risk. The competitive escalation makes the immediate retention threat more acute, and inherited evidence supports acquisition and revenue lift in this exact segment. Keep the test small and guarded because promotional pricing previously materially reduced 30-day retention; judge success on incremental retained qualified revenue and longer-term retention, not near-term conversion alone.
